TORONTO SCEPTRES ANNOUNCE HOME OPENER DECEMBER 8 AT COCA-COLA COLISEUM

Home Opener Tickets on Sale at 11 a.m. ET; Full Schedule Release on Friday

Share:

TORONTO – The Toronto Sceptres today announced its 2026-27 Professional Women’s Hockey League (PWHL) regular-season home opener will be played on Tuesday, Dec. 8 at 7 p.m. ET against PWHL Hamilton, marking an exciting return to Coca-Cola Coliseum for the inaugural matchup of a new neighbouring rivalry. The Sceptres home opener is presented by Canadian Tire Corporation.

The Sceptres will make their regular-season debut on the road on Sunday, Dec. 6, at 2 p.m. ET against their other provincial rivals, the Ottawa Charge, at Canadian Tire Centre as part of the PWHL’s opening weekend that features all 12 teams in action. The complete regular-season schedule will be announced on Friday, Oct. 2.

Tickets are on sale at 11 a.m. ET through Ticketmaster for the Sceptres home opener and can be purchased online here. Fans interested in multiple games can purchase Season Ticket Memberships and Half Packs, offering the best value and benefits. Flex packs will also be made available in all PWHL markets with the full schedule release. For more information, visit thepwhl.com/tickets. Fans can also stay up to date on detailed ticketing information by signing up for the Official Sceptres Newsletter, The Beacon, here, opens in a new tab.

The PWHL and CBC/Radio-Canada today announced the historic return of CBC’s Hockey Night in Canada that will provide comprehensive coverage for eight primetime PWHL games, including pre- and post-game panel analysis and accompanying digital content on cbcsports.ca and social media. Staying true to tradition, each Hockey Night in Canada game will feature a Canadian-based team. All national broadcast details will be announced as part of Friday’s schedule release.

ABOUT TORONTO SCEPTRES

Toronto Sceptres is one of 12 teams in the Professional Women’s Hockey League (PWHL), which was founded in 2023. The PWHL began its inaugural season in January 2024 and features the best women’s hockey players in the world. The PWHL has broken multiple attendance records and holds the worldwide record for a women’s hockey game. For the latest news and information on Toronto Sceptres, visit toronto.thepwhl.com or follow the team on Facebook, Instagram, and X. Follow the league on all social media platforms @thepwhlofficial.
